items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: he introduced himself to Benny Carter and we all went to the band room... His name was Baron Timothy Rosenkranktz... Timmie (as he was later to become known)

ctx.x: When we came off the bandstand, he introduced himself to Benny Carter and we all went to the band room to play our usual ten cent tonk which we did to pass the time between sets, as I had done on the back stairs of the Roseland ballroom with Russell's band.

Benny brought the fellow into the room and introduced him to us. His name was Baron Timothy Rosenkranktz and he was from Denmark. We later found out that he was a jazz fan and knew a lot about some of the big swing bands and the musicians. But Benny's was the first negro band he had heard in New York because he had only been in the city a couple of days when he learned that Benny had a band at the Empire ballroom. Timmie (as he was later to become known) had come to the ballroom in full dress because that was the…

The next night he was back again but dressed like an ordinary human being! When we finished the night Timmie wanted to go up to Harlem, so Linden Mills the trumpeter we called Link, took Timmie up town. Link smoked reefers and he was the one who introduced the stuff to Timmie who became so fascinated with Harlem that he finally moved there.
